doc.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: Herbie Hancock's Maiden Voyage and Speak Like a Child
summary: Carter praises Speak Like a Child and recalls Maiden Voyage being rehearsed two days and recorded in one.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: A couple with Herbie Hancock — “Maiden Voyage” and “Speak Like a Child.”

Well I’m sorry he doesn’t really like “Speak Like a Child” anymore, because they were really fabulous. They really showed his ability to encapsulate an emotion with more than three players. But for whatever reason he decided that he’s done that already. He’s gone on to other things that are just as interesting and productive. To me, there’s a chance to play some really well written music by a guy who I’m really close to. And I regret that he hasn’t done more of that. “Maiden Voyage” was fun. We rehearsed it two days at a rehearsal hall and went to the studio and made the record in one day.
